Solution 1 is correct: the limit is 1/10.

**Structure.** A vertex of T₂(Pₙ) is a pair (a,b) with 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n. Moving one token along an edge of Pₙ changes a or b by ±1, so the graph is the square grid graph restricted to the triangular region R = {(a,b) : 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n}. It has C(n,2) ≈ n²/2 vertices.

**Lower bound.** Every closed neighborhood has at most 5 vertices, so γ ≥ |R|/5 = C(n,2)/5.

**Upper bound.** On the infinite grid, the set {(x,y) : 2x + y ≡ 0 mod 5} is a perfect dominating set. Restrict it to R. Only vertices on the boundary of R, which has O(n) vertices, can lose their dominator. Adding those boundary vertices to the set costs O(n) more, so γ ≤ C(n,2)/5 + O(n).

**Limit.** Combining the bounds gives γ = n²/10 + O(n), so γ/n² → 1/10.

**Other solutions.**
- Solution 2 cites an unsupported "n²/8" pattern. This contradicts the lower bound C(n,2)/5 ≈ n²/10 only in the sense that its asserted value is larger than the true one, and the proven upper bound n²/10 + O(n) rules out 1/8.
- Solution 3 claims D₀ is a dominating set, but a vertex in D₁ has a neighbor in D₀ only if the move happens to be available. The resulting 1/6 is only an upper bound and is not tight, since 1/10 < 1/6.

CHOICE: 1
